title: Notes of Ministry - 93 - August 1980

source.file: Various/Notes of Ministry - 93 - August 198 (2503)/Notes of Ministry - 93 - August - Various.epub

paragraphs.text: The verse we have read in John 3 is one of the grand statements of Scripture as to the Person of Christ—“The Father loves the Son, and has given all things to be in his hand”. I want to say something as to what is committed to the hand of Christ. Particularly at the end of the dispensation, the Spirit of God would rally the affections of the saints back to the Person Himself that we should realize that this is not simply an historic fact but a current truth that the Father has committed all things into the hand of one Man. In fact, God has removed every other man. In the death of Christ every other man has judicially gone from the sight of God.
One Man remains, that is Christ, and the Father has committed all things to be in His hand.
Are any uncertain? Are any troubled by the difficulties and pressures of this time? Allow your gaze to come back to the centre of divine operations administratively.

We have already spoken of one key position, the fact that the Son is in the bosom of the Father. That is a key position taken up, and governs the whole of the dispensation, involving the resources in divine affection that will sustain the saints and carry them through. Now in John 3: 35 we have a key position administratively. The Lord has taken it up. The Father has taken up a position in relation to Him who is the Son and it is a position that remains. It is a position that stands to this day, despite all the failure publicly.

All that has come into the history of the church, the professing system, could never affect relations between divine Persons Themselves, and, therefore, what remains at the end is the assurance of the skill and the personal touch of the great Administrator.

You will recall that at the end of that long psalm. Psalm 78, a psalm which deals extensively with the history of the children of Israel, outlining their failures, showing the points at which they departed from the will of God for them, the psalmist comes back to speak of David and says, “And he fed them according to the integrity of his heart, and led them by the skilfulness of his hands” (Psalm 78: 72). Dear brethren, I have an impression that we need to come back in our own souls to the assurance that the skilfulness of the hand of Christ is to be seen at the end of the dispensation. It is God’s pleasure that it shall be so; not that this gift shall shine more than another; not that one servant shall become more prominent as able to help the saints into the truth: thank God for those who do help us; may we value them more!—where would we be without those who have laboured so extensively among us? but, dear brethren, what is vital is the touch personally of the hand of Christ.

So I refer to the man in chapter 9. It is very interesting that the Lord gives this man so much of His attention. How much is committed to the hands of the Son, and yet He is prepared to spend this amount of time in relation to one person. What for? In order that the works of God should be manifested in him. How wonderful that the Lord Jesus should develop in detail the works of God in relation to one person. Chapter 8 has shown how all the opposition can be overthrown. In that chapter the opposition arrays itself against Christ, and the simple assertion of the greatness of His Person overthrows the whole thing. What is needed, dear
brethren, if there are opposing elements, is the simple assertion of the truth of who Christ is.

The opposition is settled immediately. It says, “He passed on”; He was not diverted by the problems that arose, “He passed on”; and the Lord is gloriously moving on in an uninterrupted, deliberate way among the saints in the present dispensation, and He is looking for persons—may we say, He is looking for available material?—in order that the works of God shall become manifest. The Father had been there before, of course. Jesus saw this man and He saw that the hand of the Father had acted in relation to him in sovereign grace in view of his being responsive to the call and the touch of Christ.

It is a wonderful thing that the Lord Jesus in manhood linked on with what the Father was doing. How perfect He was as a Servant! He came in not as One who was originating everything—to speak carefully as to the blessed Person of the Lord Jesus. He came in in perfect manhood as linking on with what had gone before. May we be prepared if in any measure we serve to link on with what has gone before. Remember what the Lord Jesus said to those disciples in chapter 4 of this book—“I have sent you to reap that on which ye have not laboured”, (John 4: 38). That has often impressed me. The Lord was bringing the disciples in, the apostles—you might have said they were going to originate something in relation to the great system of christianity—but His word is, “I have sent you to reap that on which ye have not laboured”. “Others have laboured”. Think of all that had gone on in Old Testament times, the Father working, the Father operating in view of the great thoughts of God being set on.
I think God would cause us to be very cautious in relation to any claim to have originated anything.

If we do anything among the brethren, let it be that we are linking on with those who have gone before; only thus will it be rightly supported. So in perfection it was with the Lord Jesus Himself. He said, “My Father worketh hitherto” (John 5: 17) the Father had been doing things, and the Son in perfection links on with that in view of full results being reached. I think Mr. Taylor said that in a sense no fulness of result was reached in Old Testament times.

It was a sowing time. It was a time of the setting on of the great thoughts of God; but when we come to the New Testament, as Jesus comes in, what is in view is completion, reaching the great objectives that were in the divine mind.

So the Lord in perfection has to do with this blind man; “He spat on the ground and made mud of the spittle, and put the mud, as ointment, on his eyes”. I just want you to ponder for a moment the hands into which God had committed everything being involved in such detail in regard of one man. “He spat on the ground”—a touch no doubt as to the essence of His humanity, God manifest in flesh, who Jesus was, who He is, we may say—and then He makes ointment and actually puts it on the man’s eyes. I believe that the hands that are sustaining everything for God are active in the developing of personality among the saints at the present time, distinctive personality, for if His hand enters into it, the touch must be a distinctive one. God intends that everything for His pleasure ultimately will receive character from the hand of Christ. It is the mystery of God’s will according to Ephesians—“to head up all things in the Christ” (Ephesians 1: 9, 10). So if He is having to do with us—and thank God He is—the Man of the gospels is not an historic Jesus to those who know Him; He is One who is actively moving among the saints, coming in and going out among us, having to do with us personally
in all the pressures of the way. What He has in mind is formation that the works of God may be manifested in us.

The book of life will be full of names. Those names do not simply involve a record of persons who have been redeemed by the blood of Jesus; they involve formation, all the result of what has derived in character from the hand of Christ. I love to think of the hand of Jesus being involved in everything in which God takes pleasure. You have the type of it in Genesis.

Pharaoh gave everything into Joseph’s hand; “Without thee shall no man lift up his hand or his foot”, Genesis 41: 44. It is interesting that it is put in that way, “without thee”; in other words, every movement was to be with Joseph; he was to give character to it. So Isaiah says,

“The pleasure of Jehovah shall prosper in his hand”, (Isaiah 53: 10). That is what is going to characterize the universe of God in a day that is coming, and that is what is prospering among the saints of the assembly in our time.
Zechariah 4 gives us this typical touch as to the One who is going to finish things for God.
Zerubbabel was the governor. This is written in a day of recovery after very great departure.

We do not need to enter into the detail for that to find an echo in the experiences of the brethren. How extensive the departure has been! And yet the recovery is very wonderful, and what is governing it at this point is the hands of the one who laid the foundation. Do you not see that all that is for the pleasure of God and particularly, may I say, at the end of the time, at the end of the day, is to find its source in the hand of Christ? Let us not get out of touch with Him! You may feel persuaded in a certain way. Do not get out of touch with Christ! Maybe you feel you

have an accurate knowledge of the truth. Do not get out of touch with Him! The hands that have laid the foundation are the hands that are going to bring in the finishing touches, and I think finish here means more than simply finality; it is the finish that a craftsman can bring in to a piece of workmanship, that is the character of the Lord’s final service at the end of the dispensation.

Are we going to miss it? Zechariah had to be wakened out of sleep in order that he should see this. This is an awakening time. He saw “a lamp-stand all of gold” (Zechariah 4: 2). I trust that every person here in some sense has been awakened to see at the end something that is entirely of God, something in which the hand of man has had no place, from which man’s mind has been entirely excluded. He wakened to see “a lamp-stand all of gold”.
Then he is brought to realize the power by which what is of God is sustained, “Not by might, nor by power, but by my Spirit, saith Jehovah of hosts”. The resources of the Spirit remain.

And then his gaze is brought to bear directly on Zerubbabel whose hands are going to finish things. Oh that we should be more fully aware of the glory of the present finishing time. The Lord has initiated things; He Himself will conclude them.

Another point that is most important in this section is that what Zerubbabel is doing is building. It is very important to see that the hand of Christ, as active in these days, is active constructively. It is not simply the repair of what has been broken down; some of us

were reading in Nehemiah recently and what is stressed in that book is repair. Thank God for all that has been repaired. We look around and may feel that the devastation in days gone by has been great, but thank God for the repair work that has been done, the touch of the hand of Christ has been in it. But this is not simply repair. This is building. This is the construction positively of what is of God, and, dear brethren, this has gone on right from the beginning.

He has never ceased to operate in His own way in view of something being secured as a finished product available in relation to the service of God. The Spirit of God would recall us then to what has been initiated and sustained by the hand of Christ.

One of the most distinctive things that the Lord had initiated is the Supper. Man has had no place in that; He brought it in. It is wonderful that we have an opportunity at the beginning of each week to have part in something that has originated in the hand of Christ. He gave the loaf to His disciples. I think that gives it a wonderfully personal touch. Think of that hand that will yet govern the universe for God as engaged in giving the emblems into the hands of His disciples. One of the greatest privileges of the time of the Supper is that it consolidates the personal link that the saints have with Christ. It is at that moment that we prove His initiative as at no other time. So He has set on the Supper, He has laid the foundation in that sense, and He will finish it. What will the finish be? What touches of glory, what touches of undisclosed wealth spiritually, are yet to be entered upon? The book of Revelation speaks of Christ’s new name, something which in its fulness is yet to be disclosed. There is something yet to be manifested as to the glory of Jesus. These additional touches will ensure that the saints are rightly
available to Christ in keeping with the finish which, under the touch of His hand, is to be a glorious one.

I read in 1 Corinthians 15 not to say much about it. Who could say much about a passage such as this? What is in view in this passage is the day of eternity. It says, “Then the end, when he gives up the kingdom ...”. This is the great answer to the Father committing all things into the hands of the Son. Has anything been lost? His hand has proved trustworthy all the way through, and now it is causing everything to yield back in relation to the glory of God. His personal touch will be on the kingdom which He gives up to the Father. He will impart character to it. Nothing but what He imparts character to would be pleasing to the Father. Nothing could be pleasing to Him if it were out of keeping with the humanity that has given so much delight to heaven. And so His service is carried right through to this glorious conclusion, the work of subjugation completed—oh how much subjugation is needed! The Lord is currently acting in a subduing way, as the true David, causing persons to come under His sway in this the time of grace. How wonderful present opportunities are to come under His touch positively. The time of subjugation will not go on for ever. To think that it would go on for ever is to imply that lawlessness will still prevail. Far be the thought! A time will come when the work of subjugation which the Lord Jesus has undertaken will be fully completed and all will be in accordance with His own supremacy; He will then give the kingdom up to Him who is God and Father.

Does not such a scripture cause your affections to well out, that you already know this Person? Paul speaks of “those that are the Christ’s”; are you not glad you belong to Him? The world is making its bid, especially for the young. At this

time the world is searching for a man who can control things, who can administer rightly. Are you not glad that you belong to Christ?—“Those that are the Christ’s at his coming”. That includes more than the assembly; it includes every family, earthly and heavenly. They all belong to Christ—“those that are the Christ’s”—and, all having been brought into accord with Him, then He Himself is placed in subjection “to him who put all things in subjection to him, that God may be all in all”. What the supremacy of God will be!
‘Onward we gaze to the dawn of eternity,
Moved are our souls as we think of the Son
Taking that place of eternal subjection,
Glorious proof that His work is now done’.
(From ‘The Answering Glory’. G.H.S.Price)

Oh, if you need encouragement, dear brother or sister, let it be the assurance that things are still in the hand of Christ. There will be no failure; there could not possibly be failure. He is carrying through everything and there will be a touch of perfection according to Himself in what He gives up to the Father, that God Himself may be all in all. May we be encouraged, therefore, for His name’s sake.
I would like to say a word as to this question

in Isaiah 21, “Watchman, what of the night?” We know that the name Dumah involves silence, involving silence Godward. We are living in a world where largely there is silence Godward, dear brethren. Even in what professes His name, there is largely silence Godward.

We would feel such conditions. Indeed I think we would be urgent in prayer with God that His hand may be over the present testimony until the end. Paul says, “I exhort ... that supplications, prayers, intercessions ... be made for ... kings and all that are in dignity”, 1 Timothy 2: 1, 2. We need to be urgent in prayer for government as bearing on the testimony.

One thing in which I think God finds peculiar pleasure is assembly prayer. He listens to it, you might say, very diligently. Of course God listens diligently to every prayer. You could not think otherwise of God. But He finds peculiar interest in assembly prayer. Therefore there is a need to be diligent in prayer in relation to conditions that are around us. There is such a tide of evil which soon will be released when the church is gone. But we need to pray for its restraint until that time.

The cry goes out therefore in such conditions as we are in today and it would go out to responsible persons in local assemblies, “Watchman, what of the night?” The Lord may ask us in the place in which I am, or in which you are, “Watchman, what of the night?” The point I should like to draw attention to is the immediate answer the watchman gives here. The watchman said, “The morning cometh”. It does not matter how dark the night, dear brethren, what is immediately in view is the morning. We need to labour in our local assemblies keeping the morning before us, a morning without cloud, when Christ Himself will come, the glorious appearing of our Lord Jesus Christ. We are soon to see Him. We shall see Him face to face.

But the cry goes out now, “What of the night?” If the Lord asked me that in the place in which I am set, maybe the first thing I would say would be, ‘Well, it is dark, and there are not many left’. But that is not what the watchman is saying here, and I think the Lord is looking for persons who have their eyes fixed upon His coming, who find themselves governed in the scene of the testimony by the coming of the Lord. It has been said, as to the world to come,

‘of which we do not speak enough’. It is something that needs to be kept continually before us, that the Lord is about to come. It is not a moment for sitting down calculating how many more weeks there are, or how many years; some persons are doing that to their own loss; but for keeping our eyes on the Person who is coming. It is not just an event. It will be the greatest event that the believer could look forward to; but it is not exactly the event, it is the Person. May the Lord tune our affections, beloved, to be looking for His coming.

The cry is, “What of the night?” How are we continuing in view of that time? How are things being maintained in local assemblies until that time? What answer would He get in responsible persons if He raised this question today, “What of the night?” You might say, ‘Well, I had not really thought about it’. Let none of us be indifferent as to the way the testimony may move, or the way the Lord may move among His own. I believe the Lord would stir up our affections to be actively ready for Him at any moment. May that govern us in our local assemblies. There is need for us to keep Him personally before the saints, in the minds and affections of the brethren. The Spirit would help us to keep the Lord and His coming actively before the saints. We are at the

moment when the Spirit and the bride say ‘Come’. I believe that there is that call already in the affections of those who are near to Christ. Would that there was greater development with us of bridal affection for Christ.
Paul says, “I have espoused you unto one man, to present you a chaste virgin to Christ”, 2

Corinthians 11: 2. I think what Paul had in view at Corinth, whilst it would include what Corinth would be for Christ then, was also what the Lord would find when He came to take His own to be with Himself. Beloved, do I labour in my local assembly with that end in view? Is that the object of any part or any service that we may take on? It may be a word in the ministry meeting, it may be our part in the prayer meeting. Is it in view of a chaste virgin being here for Christ? Paul laboured for that. You might say to Paul, “What of the night?” I think Paul would immediately say, “The morning cometh”. His service had that in view.

What he did was directed to securing for Christ, finally when He comes, and at the present time, an answer for His own affections. Well, beloved, if there is to be an answer then, we would be ready that there should be an answer now.

We shall have the Lord’s coming before us tomorrow as we assemble, if we are not taken before. We may well be in glory, beloved, before the Supper. What a wonderful thing that would be? We may be with Christ actually. But if not, we shall have the experience of His coming to us tomorrow. As He comes in at the Supper to local gatherings, what does He find? I think He finds what is peculiarly attractive to Himself. It is to that that He comes. It has been said, of course, that He comes to what is of Himself. That must always be attractive.
Beloved, may that be more in expression

as we have His coming before us in our affections. The cry goes out, “Watchman, what of the night?” I think the Spirit would give us liberty to use this scripture to awaken desire in our affections that there may be something here for the affections of our Lord, that there may be true assembly conditions in which He can confide and in which He can rest.

The question goes out elsewhere, “When the Son of man comes, shall he indeed find faith on the earth?”, Luke 18: 8. He will find it, dear brethren, and He will find assembly conditions suited to Himself. It must be so because of the presence here of the Spirit. Hence the need for us not to look exactly at the darkness that is around us, and the departure, although we would feel it before God, and in that sense would eat the sin-offering in relation to what has come into the testimony; but the need ever is to keep our eye on the goal which is before us. No doubt Paul had more against him than we have ever had, or are ever likely to have, for he filled up that which was behind of the tribulations of Christ in his flesh (see Colossians 1: 24); but Paul had, as perhaps no other has had, a sense of what the glory of Christ’s coming will be. Beloved, let us keep it before us. Paul says, “Not that I have already obtained the prize ... but I pursue”, Philippians 3: 13. We need to pursue therefore, “looking towards the goal, for the prize of the calling on high of God in Christ Jesus” (verse 14). That is the object of our pursuit, not to make a place here, to make a name—that has been removed anyway in the death of Jesus—but the pursuit is in relation to Christ and in relation to Him personally.
So the watchman says, “The morning cometh”. We know that at Dumah the judgment was to come also, so he says “and also the night”. But for those that have their faith in Christ, the morning will

come and no longer the night. He will come out in His glory. It says, “Thus we shall be always with the Lord”, 1 Thessalonians 4: 17. The night will completely recede. As Christ’s glory comes in, the radiancy of His outshining will expel the night. Beloved, what a moment it will be!

Well, the cry goes out, “Watchman, what of the night?” You would see the watchman standing on the wall and looking out to see if there was someone coming, looking for the morning star, (he would be the first to see it; he would be able to tell others about it), looking also for the sun-rising. How glorious that is! The watchman would see it. Persons in the city might still be in bed, but the watchman would see it. May the Lord give us to develop in the features of watchmen. The watchman sees afar. He sees one running. God has set watchmen.

It says in this very book, “I have set watchmen upon thy walls, Jerusalem” (Isaiah 62: 6). I think they are persons who see the glory of what God has in view in the present dispensation in relation to the assembly; persons are there and they see it. May we be helped to lift up our eyes and see the grandeur of what God is about to bring in, see the glory of it as related to the places in which He has set us at the moment, that there is a glory relating to each local assembly which is peculiarly for the heart of Christ.

Now in 2 Corinthians 5 Paul has the Lord’s coming before him. He says, “We are zealous, whether present or absent, to be agreeable to him”. We need to be exercised, dear brethren, to be agreeable to Him. It says, “For we must all be manifested before the judgment-seat of the Christ”. I should like to make it clear, particularly to those who are younger, that the judgment-seat of Christ does not involve penalty. The penalty has been borne, of course, by Jesus. Nor does it

involve your eternal salvation. Paul says his desire is “to be agreeable to him”. I do not think Paul desired to be agreeable to Him through fear of judgment, but out of his affection for Christ. Now there is nothing greater, in one sense, in your life than to be agreeable to Christ.

We ought to do the things that are pleasing to Him. We have read today of His doing the things that pleased the Father (see John 8: 29). He pleased the Father in everything. The Father’s satisfaction was full in relation to Christ. There was never a moment when the Lord Jesus did anything which was not agreeable to Him. That could not be thought of. The Father was fully satisfied in Jesus. We too should do the things that are agreeable to Him. It is a sobering thing that when the Lord takes His own we shall pass by way of the judgment-seat into the day of the Lord. We shall stand before Him. Paul says we shall be manifested before the judgment-seat of Christ. It is not intended to create fear, but I think it is intended to create exercise. The bearing of that is available to us at any time, to stand before Jesus, to let Him search us, maybe to search our motives, to search our actions, as David could call upon Him to do, to see that what is there is agreeable to Him, and to get His view of every matter.

Is that our desire, beloved? How much He has done for us! What He has done could never be measured. The greatness of the work of Christ in relation to each of us personally, how great it is. How much more then should we, through affection for Christ, do the things that are agreeable to Him? We may sometimes say, ‘I shall just do this, it does not matter’. Dear brethren, am I acting as agreeable to Him? You say, ‘How do I know?’ The way in which we know is to live near to Him. To give a simple illustration, a boy at home does

not always need to be told what he must or must not do, because he knows the things that are agreeable to his father, because he lives in his company. It is intended, beloved, that we should live in the company of Jesus. Finally we shall live with Him eternally. We shall be for ever with the Lord. There will never then be the need for anything to be adjusted. There will never then be the need for protection from evil influences around us. The pathway of responsibility will be complete. I believe the Lord would cause us in the present time to value the path of responsibility, not to see it as onerous, but to value it, to see that the Lord is working something out in our souls, oftentimes through mixed conditions around us, maybe through exercises relating to health and other things. The Lord works out His way with us, but, beloved, in it He is securing an answer to Himself in that persons are being formed to be agreeable to Him.

So Paul says finally, “We must all be manifested before the judgment-seat of the Christ, that each may receive the things done in the body”. I believe that does involve that the Lord will measure our path of responsibility here in view of our place in the kingdom. The Lord has not set before us things which are impossible, but we have been given the Spirit in order that we might attain to these things, that we might walk in the steps that are pleasing in the sight of Christ.
In 1 Corinthians 15 Paul is looking forward to the end. What is in view is God being all in all.

God must be His own end in all that He has done. He will be His own end. It has been said that God will reach His end because God’s end is God. He will reach His end, beloved. He will secure everything in glory. It will not be secured in weakness, it will be secured in glory.
It will be secured as equal to God’s own thoughts in purpose.

How wonderful that is! God has not been defeated, and at the judgment-seat of Christ we shall see everything in relation to the present testimony as God sees it. There has been a reason for everything. God has allowed things of which He has not been the author, but He has allowed them, I think, in order that there might be created in us exercise to continue to be faithful to Him until the coming of the Lord.

We shall see all things then clearly. We shall know as we are known. We shall see the glory of what God has in view for Himself when He shall rest in His love and joy over His own with singing. What a wonderful thing it will be when, without the hindrances which we find in us and around us, we shall view God’s ways from His own side. But Paul here says, “For he must reign until he put all enemies under his feet”. He must reign, dear brethren. It is a necessity of God that Christ must reign. Here in the scene in which He has been rejected and cast out, where persons have said, “Away with him”. He must reign. What a reign it will be! I would encourage those who are younger to be bold in your testimony for Christ. You might be the only person in the classroom or in the office who stands by the name of Jesus, but finally you will be associated with the One who will reign. You might say, ‘I do not feel very strong in giving testimony to Christ’. But stand by His name, because finally you will be associated with the One who must reign.

It does not look like it at the moment when you think of the problems that there are in the world, the anxieties that are upon the spirits of men. .How vast they are! When Christ comes out in His glory to reign everything will be set in its place. What a reign it will be! Evil will then be scattered. The One who comes out will scatter

evil with His eyes (see Proverbs 20: 8). “The earth shall be filled with the knowledge of the glory of Jehovah as the waters cover the sea”, Habakkuk 2: 14. He will put into effect in His reign in the world to come what He has done in His death for God’s pleasure. But the wonderful thing is that we have the earnest of that in our hearts already. Therefore I believe it would help us and govern us in the time in which we are, in the night season, to live in the outshining of the reign of Christ. He reigns in the affections of the saints now. That is not future, beloved. “He must reign” in its fulness relates to what is future, but He reigns in the affections of the saints now. May we make greater room for Him to reign in our lives! There will not be a problem in the world to come that He will not be able to resolve, and in our lives now the reign of Christ can be as effective as it will be in the day to come.

Let us make way for Him. Let our affections expand in relation to Jesus. “He must reign until he put all enemies under his feet”. Everything will be brought into subjection to Christ. There will not be a single insubject element left; the enemy himself is finally to be confined, and death annulled. Think of the glory of it! Christ will bring in a universe which will be entirely for God’s satisfaction. You might say, “Watchman, what of the night?” These things would stir us in our affections. Sometimes the picture looks very dark, but it is not all dark. There are exercises to carry in the testimony, the burdens the Lord would place upon us, but let us face them and carry them in the light of the glory of what is about to dawn upon our view, Christ Himself. May the Lord encourage us therefore. All things will be brought into subjection to Him and then He Himself will be placed in subjection to Him who put all things in subjection to Him, that God may be all in all. Everywhere you look in that eternal day what will be
seen will be the outshining of God. Everywhere in the affections of men what will be seen will be the supremacy of God.

Beloved, these things are intended to set our hearts on fire, to stimulate us in the time of testimony in view of the time when we shall share the glory, when we shall be with Him in the reigning time, and then, finally, when there will be conditions where God will tabernacle with men. Think of God tabernacling with men, finding delight in dwelling amongst creatures, among persons who have known and proved His love, and being their God. What a wonderful thing that will be that God will tabernacle with men. I think it involves that there will be something peculiarly distinctive in the bringing in of the eternal day of which it is said, “Behold, the tabernacle of God is with men”. There will be a knowledge of Himself that will crown the knowledge the saints have had of Him throughout the testing time, and all will be brought through to the glory of the outshining of God in His own realm. No doubt it is linked with the word to the overcomer in Philadelphia, “I will write upon him the name of my God, and the name of the city of my God ... and my new name”, Revelation 3: 12. May the Lord stimulate us, therefore, dear brethren, to have the morning before us, to keep the outshining of Christ before us, and to let that shining have its effect in our lives and in our local assemblies, so that there may be conditions here with which He will be pleased when He comes. May it be so, for His name’s sake.

articles.title: “I AM THE RESURRECTION AND THE LIFE”
articles.author: D. A. Burr
articles.meeting: Word at the burial of Mrs, J. S. Pugh

paragraphs.text: The period since our sister has been taken has provided an opportunity for reflection over the word, and this scripture, to which our brother referred in prayer, has been in my mind. What has affected me about it is that, when the Lord comes into any matter. He does so in a way that is perfectly suited to the circumstances into which He comes—and when He comes, He comes in fully. He comes in personally. Like our sister, Lazarus was taken ill and his sisters, as we, assured of the Lord’s interest and concern, took the matter to Him. What a wonderful thing that is, that in this matter that came amongst them they were ready to bring the Lord in—not that the Lord responded by coming in immediately, but no doubt His interest was very fully aroused by what happened. He allowed it to go further, as He has done amongst us; and then He came in. I think the Lord would give us an experience in this occasion of His coming in, and in a way that is wholly suited to the circumstances which He enters.
Martha was found with a measure of faith, and He came where Martha was—think of that!

What a wonderful thing! Martha, you might say, had a lot to learn, but Jesus came where Martha was. And we, no doubt, have a lot to learn, but the Lord has come where we are and He has it in mind that we should gain some fresh experience of Himself. The Lord in conversation with Martha brings out from her how far she was in her understanding. She had apprehended that there was to be a resurrection in the last day, and we have apprehended it; we are assured of it

and it is a source of comfort to us. But the Lord says that there is something that is greater than the resurrection in the last day; there is a glorious Person who is “the resurrection and the life”. Not ‘will be’; not exactly that He assumes the office of One who brings in the resurrection in the last day, but He is the resurrection and the life.

We may think of other circumstances—think of how when He speaks about food—spiritual food in chapter 6. He says, “I am the living bread which has come down out of heaven” (John 6: 51). And now think of Him in this chapter. He says, “I am the resurrection and the life”.

Not simply that there will be a resurrection and there will be life; but “I am the resurrection and the life”. What a blessed thing that is, what an assurance to all our hearts that there is a way in which we may apprehend the Lord in any circumstances in which we may be; He has a glorious title and a moral glory which is suited to the circumstances in which we may be found. And He brings it in not simply that we might apprehend it as a fact, but that we might believe. That is why He stayed away—that these disciples might believe—and then He came in and His end is secured. What a blessed thing that is! It says at the end of this section that
“Many therefore ... believed on him”; they “saw what he had done, and believed on him”.
How blessed it is!

When He comes in He does not come and stand in the background; He comes right into the centre of the circumstances where we may be. He did not join the crowd that was there, but He joined the mourners. What a word of comfort that is! Furthermore, He did not simply come and stand alongside them, but He was with them in the sorrow in the deepest and fullest way. We had in ministry amongst us that there is something about sympathy that goes further
even than compassion, and sympathy was found with Jesus when He came into this matter.

Well, I thought we might be assured by these things that the Lord knows every circumstance in which we may be and He knows how to come into it; and He does it that we might see some glory of His and that we might believe. May this be our experience, and as believing may we know what it is to have joy in believing, as the scripture says. May He be glorified in this occasion and in this experience, for His name’s sake.

THE FATHER’S PLANTING There are some flowers which now survive only in very small numbers. A booklet ‘Britain’s Rarest Plants’ says, for example, that Bristol Rock-Cress is now found only in the Avon Gorge, while Tufted Saxifrage exists only in a few rocky areas at high altitudes in Scotland and Wales—there are probably less than a hundred plants altogether.

It makes one think of the delight God has in the quality of His work, particularly where widespread departure has left but few walking in the truth. Malachi 3: 17 shows how Jehovah cherished His “peculiar treasure” in those who feared Him, and thought upon His name, in a dark day in Israel’s history. Those same choice features were carried through more than 400
years so that they are found unimpaired in the first chapter of Luke. Then, later, the Lord expresses His pleasure in the “few” in Sardis who had not defiled their garments. So today
‘we can think of precious features of faithful-

ness in saints in many parts of the earth, plants of the heavenly Father’s planting, and the quality, beauty, and fragrance of His work in them. Hidden from public notice, all is treasured under His eye, and preserved and nourished by His grace.

We should also bear in mind that we are all at ‘the table’ on the same ground—the Lord’s death. It is the sole ground for each and all, therefore individual feelings should not be brought in. Often people are occupied with their own feelings as to the Lord’s death instead of with the death itself. The assembly is the sphere where Christ is all and in all. It is the sense of each one being at the Lord’s table on this one ground, and where consequently individuality must be dropped, that shows the wickedness of divisions. It is to be feared that we have been too ready for division in the spirit of our minds. Separation is a last resource when evil is irremediable. In regard to fellowship we maintain that the Lord is with us; if evil arises, the question arises, is it such that we are assured the Lord has left, for until this is the case we have no ground for leaving. Evil coming in does not drive the Lord out; it is when it is sanctioned that His presence is withdrawn. This is seen in the case of Achan—His presence discovered the evil, and if they did not judge it He would not be with them any more.
